newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares in bull run, Bombay up three pct.
newsitem.headline: India shares in bull run, Bombay up three pct.

text.p: ** (1345 GMT) - Indian stocks in sharp rally, benchmark
Bombay stocks index ends 122.85 points, or 2.97 pct up
** Sharp rally in index-linked stocks Hindustan Lever, HDFC
and ACC push market, foreign funds keen buyers -traders
** Speculators jump on buying bandwagon on first day of
Bombay weekly trade account, but rally not broad-based,
** National exchange index ends 22.75 pts, or 1.95 pct
higher at 1,192.40, Delhi 13.97 pts at 897.79, Madras
93.97 pts at 4,347.90 and Calcutta 4.47 pts at 125.74

Trading at the Bombay Stock Exchange got off to a delayed start at 2.00 p.m. (0830 GMT) against the normal 10.00 a.m., due to a power failure at the bourse, BSE officials said. Trading was extended by one hour to end at 4.30 p.m. (1100 GMT).
"It is a very strong market. There has been general buying," said Prashant Purker, head of institutional sales at Peregrine Capital India in Bombay.

Cement stocks were in favour due to the changing market outlook on the sector, traders said. Shares of Associated Cement Companies (ACC) jumped 62.50 rupees to 1,452.50 and India Cements rose 9.75 rupees to 108.0.
"People are finding cement stocks cheap, perhaps because the market is becoming expensive," Peregrine's Purker said.
Gujarat Ambuja Cement continued its uptrend, adding 17.50 rupees at 346.50 on market rumours of a possible bonus share issue by the firm. Company officials would not comment.
The market's recent sharp rally might lure profit takers in the short-run before the next upward charge, traders said.

"We are due for a small reaction. The market seems to be overbought," ITC Threadneedle's Srinivasan said. "But, macro factors such as the bank rate cut are driving it up. There is increasing liquidity in the market."
